sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Soundscape Licensing and Audio Sample Subscriptions

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary state without sub-state corporate registries)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (1962, as amended by the 1996, 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
Luxembourg-Germany Income and Capital Tax Convention (1991, as amended by the 2009 Protocol and the OECD MLI)
Luxembourg-France Income and Capital Tax Convention (revision signed 2018; effective for fiscal years from 2019)
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 1994; as amended by subsequent protocols)
OECD/G20 Multilateral Instrument (MLI) ratified by Luxembourg and applicable to covered tax agreements
European Union Treaty freedoms of establishment and free movement of capital applicable to EU/EEA shareholders

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (2004 AML/CFT Law), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 12 July 2024 aligning access with ECJ case C-37/20 and restricting public access to authorities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; Law of 5 August 1993 on the financial sector governing regulated professionals acting as the SCSp's AML gatekeepers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card copy of each natural person UBO and of the SCSp's designated manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the UBO's country of residence; certification by a civil-law notary or certified public translator in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the country of issuance is a 1961 Hague Conference member; otherwise consular legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and latest extract from the trade register for each corporate UBO or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, US Secretary of State, Crossroads Bank for Enterprises in Belgium)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the issuing registry's signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or existence certificate for each corporate UBO or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or tax authority of the corporate UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account history, conduct and signatory authority of the UBO or gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal banking institution of the UBO or gérant, whether Luxembourg-based or foreign
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or legalization of the bank's notarized signature where the bank is located in a non-EU jurisdiction; EU banks may deliver by authenticated bank mail or signed letter under CSSF-accepted practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Judicial or criminal record extracts of UBOs and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court or central criminal records authority in the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The 2004 AML/CFT Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02 require identification of politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, with mandatory screening against (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Council Regulations (EC) 881/2002, (EC) 2580/2001, (EU) 269/2014 and amending regimes), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists as implemented by EU law, (iii) Luxembourg's national freezing lists issued by the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, and (iv) contractually, because the business relies on Stripe and PayPal as US payment rails, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Sectoral Sanctions Identification (SSI) lists. Commercial screening databases covering global PEPs must be used at thresholds consistent with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. All UBOs, gérants, counterparties and beneficial owners of future distributions must be screened and the results documented in the AML file prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - official gateway at https://www.lbr.lu; the LBR is the legal successor of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with electronic filing and certified extraction services; administrative access is also available via guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings are accepted in French and German, with French prevailing in registry practice; the registered name must be expressed in Latin/Roman script including required diacritics for Luxembourgish, French or German; any non-Latin-script commercial name (CJK, Cyrillic, Greek or Arabic) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the incorporation deed, and the transliterated form becomes the name of record; the LBR applies a distinctiveness test preventing confusion with earlier-registered names and protected trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Crédit - requires prior authorization from the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
Assurance, Réassurance - requires prior authorization from the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA)
SICAV, SICAF, Fonds de placement, OPCVM - CSSF authorization required under investment-fund legislation
Société Nationale, Administration publique, Chambre de Commerce - tokens implying State or public-institution patronage, prohibited on public-order grounds
SA, Sàrl, SCA, Société Anonyme - suffixes reserved for other corporate forms; an SCSp must use 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'SCSp'
Audit, Réviseur, Avocat, Notaire - regulated professional titles reserved to holders of the corresponding ministerial license or faculty

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; SCSp governed by Articles 308-1 et seq., inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016; registration rules under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), acting through the MyGuichet.lu electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp charter/partnership agreement (contrat de société) and RCS registration declaration, filed electronically with the Luxembourg Business Registers; an extract is published in the electronic compendium RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SCSp. The amount and form of the partners' contributions are fixed contractually in the partnership agreement; no escrow or blocked bank account is required. Contributions may be in cash or in kind, and the general partner's powers and liability profile are governed by the agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
At a meeting held on [date], the initial partners of the SCSp, having reviewed the draft partnership agreement, RESOLVED:

1. All partnership interests in the agreement are subscribed and the stated contributions are credited to capital accounts.
2. The registered office is fixed at [address] and will remain at that address for the initial fiscal period.
3. [Manager Name] is appointed gérant, and [Officer Name] is appointed authorised signatory, each acting alone, with authority to open bank accounts, enter into licensing contracts, and complete all registration formalities.
4. The gérant is authorised to file the charter with the Luxembourg Business Registers, effect RESA publication, and take every step necessary for the formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal legal preparation; optional Luxembourg notary if notarized deed is preferred; name availability checked through lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name is available. Prepare a French-language partnership agreement stating the SCSp name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose covering ISIC 5920 royalty-free music licensing and digital audio subscription activities, identity of the general partner, initial partners, contribution details, management powers, and distribution rules. The agreement may be signed in private writing unless immovable property is contributed, in which case notarization is mandatory. Authenticate signatories' Luxtrust/eID credentials for electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Statement of capital contributions in cash or in kind
Identification documents and Luxtrust/eID credentials of founding partners and managers
Consent form from the landlord for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects to the corporate name, amend the name in a corrective deed and refile; if notarized signatures are requested, arrange notarial legalization and resubmit through the same filing channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), MyGuichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to MyGuichet.lu using Luxtrust/eID. Submit the standard RCS incorporation form for an SCSp, attach the executed partnership agreement, landlord consent, and identification documents, and pay the applicable RCS filing fee. Upon validation, the RCS issues the RCS number and the national business number (matricule).
required_dossiers: Mandate or power of attorney if a Luxembourg agent files on behalf of the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS sends a query, correct the specified inconsistencies in the deed, add any required French or German translation, and refile within the response period; expedited handling may be requested in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication of the formation extract in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the SCSp is registered, LBR automatically publishes the formation extract in RESA. Monitor the publication, download the proof of publication, and retain it for banking, commercial counterparties, and tax files.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is not visible within ten business days, file a written follow-up with LBR and verify that all publication fees have been settled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Luxembourg VAT registration form with AED using the RCS extract and business description, specifying B2B/B2C cross-border digital licensing activities processed through Stripe and PayPal. Register as an employer with CCSS only when hiring staff, and keep all payroll and social declarations current from that point.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and national business number
Identity documents of managers and authorised signatories
Description of digital audio licensing model and payment platforms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AED requests additional evidence of the business model or permanent establishment, respond with a business plan, projected transaction flows, and platform revenue documentation to expedite issuance of the VAT number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des PME et de l'Entrepreneuriat, Service des autorisations d'établissement, via MyGuichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commercial activity commences, file the electronic establishment authorization application through MyGuichet.lu using NACE code 59.20 (sound recording and music publishing) and, where applicable, 63.11 (digital platform services). Provide evidence that the managers are of good repute, the RCS extract, the partnership agreement, and any supporting business description. No sectoral media or music-specific statutory license is required for royalty-free stock music distribution; this general authorization covers commercial establishment.
required_dossiers: Criminal record certificate (bulletin no. 3) of managers
Business description covering the digital licensing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requires further information or a revised business plan, submit the requested items within the stated deadline. If the authorization is refused, the applicant may appeal to the competent administrative court and may request interim relief in justified cases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Service des autorisations d'établissement for commercial establishment; Administration de l'environnement for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement – commercial establishment authorization for digital audio licensing and platform operations (NACE 59.20 / 63.11).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Environment Agency, Luxembourg Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Law of 15 May 2018; purely digital royalty-free music licensing does not fall within Annex I or Annex II EIA categories.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or substantive point-source air emissions are associated with the activity. Office premises must comply with municipal wastewater discharge bylaws, and any electronic waste must be handled through approved take-back schemes under Luxembourg WEEE regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) for office premises; structural load inspection in case of fit-out works; workplace health-and-safety registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); employer affiliation with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) where staff are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration); VAT and registration duties: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); central corporate and tax registration portal: MyGuichet.lu / https://pfi.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first appoint a local approved statutory agent and file through MyGuichet.lu for incorporation with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS). The RCS assigns a 13-digit business identification number which doubles as the corporate tax file number. VAT registration with the AEDT is mandatory where taxable activity in Luxembourg exists, resulting in an LU+8-digit VAT identification number; otherwise a separate VAT registration application is submitted via the same digital portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (SCSp is fiscally transparent by default; income is taxed at partner level)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp may elect under Article 175 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law to become subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, overriding fiscal transparency. No US-style check-the-box regime exists. The EU ATAD hybrid mismatch rules may restrict the tax benefit of transparency/opaqueness elections in cross-border scenarios.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the Luxembourg small-enterprise exemption; however, non-resident and digital suppliers have no de minimis threshold and must register from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via the Peppol infrastructure since 1 January 2024; no continuous transaction control (CTC), real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime applies to B2B invoices; Luxembourg VAT returns are filed periodically through MyGuichet.lu.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supply of digital royalty-free music licenses is an electronic service. Luxembourg VAT is not chargeable where the place of supply is outside Luxembourg: (i) B2B recipient established in a third country; (ii) B2C non-taxable recipient established outside the EU; or (iii) EU B2B recipient where the reverse charge applies in the customer's member state. Zero-rating/outside-scope treatment requires documentary evidence of the recipient's foreign establishment and absence of effective use or exploitation of the license in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: VAT invoice (or self-billing/credit note) accompanied by a place-of-supply determination narrative
Signed royalty-free stock music license agreement specifying customer, territory, usage scope and royalty/fee amount
Proof of customer's foreign status: EU VAT ID for intra-EU B2B supplies, or foreign business registration/passport for third-country supplies
Payment evidence: Stripe/PayPal settlement reports and bank statements showing actual receipt from the foreign customer
Inward remittance certificate or FX bank memo for repatriated licence fees
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess unsubstantiated zero-rated or outside-scope positions within a five-year limitation period (extended for intentional non-compliance), issuing Luxembourg VAT at the standard 17% rate plus default interest of 0.8% per month and administrative fines up to 100% of the tax evaded. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims may trigger criminal prosecution with imprisonment and additional financial penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in the Eurosystem, together with the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises banking AML/KYC conduct and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full euro-area convertible-currency status. EU Treaty provisions (Art. 63 TFEU) and the EU Capital Movements Directive guarantee unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility. No exchange-control authorisation is required for cross-border income, royalties, or profit distributions. An SCSp is tax-transparent, so profit distributions by the partnership are generally treated as direct distributions to partners and are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, provided the partners are not Luxembourg tax residents and no Luxembourg commercial or real-estate fixed base is created. Anti-hybrid (ATAD), CRS/FATCA reporting, and substance requirements must nevertheless be documented.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion applies. Export receipts and licensing-income proceeds may be retained in EUR or a foreign currency, and conversion is freely available at market rates through authorised banks. No BCL approval or repatriation deadline exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA-licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) passported into Luxembourg; Low for offshore, non-EEA digital-only EMIs. Legal constraints: Offshore EMIs cannot offer accounts or payment services to a Luxembourg SCSp unless they hold a Luxembourg/EEA authorisation or operate through a licensed branch; PSD2 (Directive 2015/2366) restricts deposit-taking and mandates client-fund safeguarding in a credit institution; the CSSF applies AML/CFT outsourcing rules (CSSF circulars 18/667, 19/732) that require a local access point, UBO identification, and transaction monitoring. Platforms such as Stripe and PayPal can be used only as payment collection fixtures connected to a licensed acquiring bank, not as the primary treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not a statutory requirement under Luxembourg law. CSSF circular 19/732 allows remote video identification and electronic signature for non-face-to-face onboarding. In practice, domestic tier-1 banks accept remote onboarding for low-risk licensing businesses, but require (i) certified true copies of the SCSp deed of formation, (ii) a banking resolution or power of attorney signed by the general partner, (iii) apostilled notarial certificates from non-EU partners, and (iv) an initial interview by video call with the beneficial owners and signatories. A physical visit may be requested by the bank's compliance committee where ultimate beneficial owners reside in high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through/transparency status of SCSp without legal personality, creating uncertainty on which UBOs must be identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement and status deed; Luxembourg RBE (beneficial ownership) registry excerpt; a UBO declaration listing every natural person exercising ultimate control; notarised GP resolution; tax-transparency opinion from a Luxembourg law firm; proof of residence and source-of-wealth documentation for each direct/indirect partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of low-ticket cross-border royalty/free-stock music revenue with remote global customers; risk-score flags for 'online content monetisation' and potential licencing rights ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial licence and royalty distribution contracts; portfolio and catalogue ownership or sub-licensing evidence; audited or internally reconciled statements from Stripe/PayPal and payment gateways; log of watermarking/usage-monitoring software; tax filings showing cost structure; standard customer KYC and merchant verification documentation under PSP due diligence; compliance with EU Digital Services Act transparency notices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and absence of Luxembourg economic substance may trigger bank suspicion of conduit financing or tax avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a physical Luxembourg office or registered agent arrangement; payroll/outsourced service contracts with local administrators; minutes of partner/GP meetings from Luxembourg; transfer pricing master file for all intercompany fees; VAT and corporate tax returns (including NIL returns); CRS/FATCA registration confirmations; forecast treasury cash-flow model proving on-going operational substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital subscriptions via SWIFT MT103 with explicit Remittance Information (field 70) using EU balance-of-payments purpose code for capital contributions (e.g., code 'CAPT'/'EQUI' at instructed banks, alternatively 'EQUI' per ISO 20022 Purpose Extensions). Use the receiving bank's BIC and the SCSp's IBAN; ensure the general partner's name and partnership registration number appear in the 50K/59F fields. For EUR payments, use SEPA Credit Transfer (E-Purpose code) or SEPA Instant for fast-clearing up to EUR 100k; for non-EUR, instruct same-day value USD/EUR/GBP via SWIFT with nostro pre-funding. Prior to booking, the bank verifies UBO register, anti-money laundering clearance, and the source of funds; for amounts > EUR 10k a copy of the capital call resolution and documentary proof of beneficial owner is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty distributions and trade settlements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103/MT202 for non-EUR and through SEPA Credit Transfer/TARGET2 for EUR. Commercial letters of credit (MT700) are limited to high-value physical-asset purchases; for music licensing services, open-account mechanics with SWIFT-gpi tracking and Net-30 settlement are standard. Payments to connected vendors are cleared via bank-facing APIs or EBICS with dual-authorisation, and each disbursement must carry either a corresponding FX collar or a natural matching of EUR income; AML reviews of recipient account histories are run against PEP/sanctions databases.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (deliverable, up to 24-month tenors) with ECB-licensed banks or broker-dealers
FX options (European style) for premium-rate risk management
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-convertibility currencies such as CNY/INR/BRL, executed under ISDA 1998 NDF terms
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matched Euro/USD cash-flow arrangements
FX swaps/rollovers on standard T+2/T+1 settlement for treasury liquidity parking

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registration particulars (annual return) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the entity's RCS registration date; no fixed calendar deadline; filing must be made within one month of the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines imposed by the RCS for late filing; persistent non-compliance may trigger judicial dissolution proceedings and strike-off from the register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of the financial statements (where applicable) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the partners; must be filed within seven months of the financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate from EUR 50 to EUR 5,000 per document; repeated default may lead to administrative strike-off and criminal fines for responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of beneficial ownership (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one month following the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 for non-compliance with UBO reporting; the RBE registrar may block access to the commercial register and impose daily penalty payments or administrative fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax return and capital duty declaration filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Income Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes - ACD) and Luxembourg VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Article 161 LIR: corporate tax returns must be filed by 31 March of the following year; extended automatic deadline to 31 December of the following year (applicable to financial year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax, plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal fines may apply for fraudulent non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return filing (if annual VAT simplification is elected for eligible small businesses)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return must be filed by 31 March following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the VAT due, plus late-payment interest of 0.5% per month; administrative tax penalty may be assessed at 20% of the outstanding amount

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg S.C.S. (SCSp) is exempt from mandatory statutory audit unless the entity exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average number of employees 25; entities forming part of a group must apply group-level assessment
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg Accounting Law transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements or voluntary adoption for individual financial statements; simplified accounting presentation rules apply to small undertakings

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually confirm its beneficial ownership information in the Luxembourg RBE registry within one month of the anniversary of registration; any transfer or change of shares or partnership interests during the year must be reported to the RBE within one month of the change; the annual confirmation maintains continuous accuracy of UBO identification for all shareholding transfers
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges and Usufruct on Partnership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - USD 2,200 per annum for registered office and corporate agent services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a full certified statutory audit; USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 for a voluntary review or DCL (Declaration du Contexte Legal) audit report if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate benchmark: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent; no entity-level corporate income tax. Luxembourg IP box grants an 80% exemption on qualifying copyright/software licensing income, reducing the effective rate to approximately 5.16%-5.40% for qualifying IP in Luxembourg City. Participation exemption and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may produce 0% dividend tax outcomes. Luxembourg's statutory loss-carryforward is unlimited; the 5-year figure in the schema is retained as an audit planning convention.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (CIT / municipal business tax / net wealth tax combined declaration) via the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal (eCIT through myGuichet); transparent SCSp partners are assessed on their allocated partnership profits
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 May following the fiscal year-end; additional extension to 31 December is available upon request; non-residents with a Luxembourg permanent establishment file on the same calendar

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: full name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg VAT ID, registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SCSp must state the general partner, limited partners, and local tax representative when a Luxembourg permanent establishment is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year: opening and closing dates of the accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident must align the return with the Luxembourg PE accounting year and attach branch financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable commercial profit or loss before allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source licensing and subscription revenue and arm's length deductions attributable to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward utilisation and IP-box deduction computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident should attach the SCSp allocation statement and substantiate any treaty relief and IP-box claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of profit or loss to partners, including tax identification numbers and capital account movements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners are generally taxed in their home jurisdiction unless the income is attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, treaty relief, and reduced withholding tax claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a Luxembourg tax residency certificate (Form 260) and treaty-specific documentation when relief is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 10%-20% of assessed tax; late-payment interest at 0.6% per commenced month; administrative fine up to €25,000; persistent non-filing triggers forced tax assessment and criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for portfolio distributions; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Luxembourg participation exemption conditions. SCSp profit allocations are tax-transparent and are not normally subject to entity-level Luxembourg dividend WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double-tax-agreement relief, the beneficial owner delivers a valid Luxembourg tax residency certificate (Form 260) and a treaty relief claim to the paying agent before distribution. If WHT has already been applied, a refund application must be filed under Article 154 LIR within the applicable limitation period, supported by ownership evidence, substance documentation, and confirmations of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic withholding tax is 0% on interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty rates vary by DTA: dividends 5%-15%, interest 0%-10%, royalties 0%-10%; no WHT applies under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for qualifying associated companies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg law does not set an explicit statutory de minimis threshold for Local File / Master File. In audit practice, material related-party transactions above EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate attract mandatory contemporaneous documentation review; consolidated group revenue above EUR 750,000,000 triggers the statutory CbC report threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations framework, but it enforces substance-over-form doctrine through Article 6 AbgrG and Article 56bis LIR, the OECD anti-BEPS principles, and anti-avoidance case law. A stock-music licensing SCSp must demonstrate real Luxembourg substance: qualified staff, active strategic and operational decision-making, a Luxembourg bank account, actual EQ-building, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Failure to prove substance may result in denial of treaty benefits and reclassification as a fully taxable resident entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of royalty-free stock music subscription revenue received through Stripe or PayPal, or fraudulent allocation of income to non-reporting foreign limited partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of omitted income; fraud surcharge of 20%-100%; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; criminal fine up to €250,000; imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and managing directors who sign or cause a false declaration to be filed are jointly and severally liable for taxes evaded; travel bans, asset seizures, director disqualification, and imprisonment may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure (Abuse of Law)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without Luxembourg substance: no local management, no physical premises, all decisions taken abroad, no employees handling licensing contracts, and diversion of royalty income through opaque partner structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax transparency and treaty benefits; reclassification as a corporate resident subject to Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; re-assessment plus 25% penalty for non-compliance with substance documentation requests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or general partners who knowingly set up a shell arrangement are personally exposed to restitution claims, tax damages, coercive collection measures, travel bans, and criminal liability for abuse of law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a Local File / Master File for related-party royalty flows and partner-level licensing arrangements above the materiality threshold, or application of non-arm's length royalty rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward TP adjustment with a 10%-20% surcharge, monthly interest at 0.6%, administrative fines up to €250,000 for non-production of records, and discretionary best-judgment assessment against the SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who obstruct transfer pricing audits face personal administrative fines; in egregious cases the corporate veil is pierced and managing partners are held personally liable for the tax difference plus accrued interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of Stripe or PayPal to process high-volume stock music licensing revenue while operating without a Luxembourg bank account, corporate substance, or verifiable ownership framework; round-trip payments, rapid withdrawals, or off-book crypto conversion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The underlying licensing activity is not itself an AML-licensed profession, but suspicious transaction reporting and AML penalties apply if the payment pattern is used to conceal tax evasion or money laundering; penalties under Luxembourg AML law may reach €1,000,000 for culpable institutions and individuals in abuse cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors may be personally criminally liable for money-laundering predicates if they direct payment flows to evade tax or intentionally obscure beneficial ownership; asset freezes and travel bans may be imposed.
